summary:
AnalogAtlas is an interactive, data-driven platform designed to identify Earth locations that resemble potential permanent Moon base sites and Mars locations. We developed MERIDIAN, a multi-evidence ranking engine that analyzes terrain, geological characteristics, and environmental processes to identify meaningful similarities beyond visual appearance.

Our platform uses open Earth-observation and planetary datasets to compare 135 locations across Earth, the Moon, and Mars. Instead of presenting information in only one format, AnalogAtlas provides several ways to explore the results. Users can view ranked lists of the closest Earth analogs, compare multiple locations side by side, explore locations through interactive maps, examine detailed similarity scores, and understand which geological or environmental features contribute to each match. The platform also provides data provenance, uncertainty estimates, and explanations to make the results more transparent and reliable. It further distinguishes between physical similarity and practical site suitability, helping users evaluate locations from different perspectives.

AnalogAtlas addresses the NASA challenge by turning complex planetary data into accessible and scientifically grounded insights. It is important because Earth can serve as a natural testing environment for studying conditions similar to those on the Moon and Mars, helping researchers explore potential challenges and support future space exploration .
details:
Project Details – AnalogAtlas

How it works:

AnalogAtlas is an interactive scientific platform that identifies Earth locations that resemble potential permanent Moon base sites and Mars locations. Its core engine, MERIDIAN (Multi-Evidence Ranking with Domain-Integrated Agreement Navigation), processes planetary datasets and compares locations using geological, topographical, and environmental features.

The platform is built around five evidence channels that evaluate different aspects of similarity. It does not simply compare images or surface appearance; it analyzes terrain characteristics, geological patterns, and environmental processes. The engine then produces ranked Earth analogs, similarity scores, uncertainty estimates, and explanations for the results.

Multiple ways to explore the results:

We designed AnalogAtlas to make complex scientific information accessible through different interactive tools:

  • Ranking: Displays the closest Earth analog locations for a selected Moon or Mars site.
  • Side-by-Side Comparison: Allows users to compare locations and understand their similarities and differences.
  • Interactive Maps: Shows the geographical distribution of analog locations.
  • Similarity Analysis: Breaks down the evidence behind each match and explains which features contribute to the result.
  • Portfolio Selection: Helps users select a complementary group of analog sites instead of relying only on the highest-ranked location.
  • Data Provenance: Provides information about the datasets and sources behind the results.
  • CSV Export: Allows users to download results for further analysis.

The platform also separates physical similarity from practical suitability, allowing users to consider factors such as terrain hazards, slope, roughness, thermal conditions, and ice context without confusing them with the similarity score.

Tools and technologies:

The scientific processing and ranking engine was developed using Python 3.11, with NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, and Scikit-learn. Pytest was used for mathematical contract testing. We worked with open scientific datasets from NASA, ESA/Copernicus, JAXA, and USGS, including elevation models, satellite observations, geological information, and crater databases. Microsoft Planetary Computer and its STAC API support additional Earth-location screening.

Creativity and innovation:

One of our main creative contributions is MERIDIAN's integration of five earlier algorithmic approaches — PRISM, CALIPER, CAPER, ORCA, and SAGE — into one unified ranking system. Instead of depending on a single similarity method, it combines multiple evidence channels and uses agreement between different ranking approaches to provide more informative results. It also communicates uncertainty and preserves data provenance, making the analysis more transparent and scientifically traceable.

Factors considered and intended impact:

During development, we considered differences in planetary data resolution, geological and terrain characteristics, environmental processes, data availability, measurement uncertainty, and the distinction between similarity and mission suitability. We also aimed to discover less familiar Earth analog environments rather than focusing only on well-known deserts and polar regions.

Our intended impact is to make planetary comparison more systematic and accessible, help researchers identify promising Earth environments for studying Moon and Mars conditions, and support future space exploration research and technology testing.
